ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: the figure is a fused benzene ring-nitrogen-containing heterocycle skeleton, with a benzene ring on the left, a carbonyl C=O at the upper right, and NH and NH labeled consecutively on the right; the tetrahedral central carbon below is connected to a negatively charged oxygen O−, and connected to an NH, which is further connected to the variable substituent R. Curved arrows are also drawn in the figure, but the problem requires ignoring these arrows. Reasoning: according to the specified method, only convert the atom-bond connectivity. Treat R as the wildcard `*`, the amine to which it is connected is written as `N`, then to the tetrahedral ring carbon is written as `C1`, and this carbon has an `[O-]` branch, giving `*NC1([O-])`. Continue along the heterocycle through `NNC(=O)`, then enter the fused benzene ring written as `c2ccccc2`, and finally use ring label `1` to close to the initial tetrahedral carbon, therefore the SMILES is `*NC1([O-])NNC(=O)c2ccccc21`.

raw_record.question_text: What is the SMILES expression of the transition-state structure shown in the image, ignoring the arrows?

method.method_draft: Ignore all curved arrows and convert only the atom-bond graph. Start at the variable substituent R as wildcard `*`, write the attached amine as `N`, then the tetrahedral ring carbon as `C1` with branch `([O-])`. Continue around the heterocycle through `NNC(=O)`, then enter the fused benzene as `c2ccccc2`, and close the fusion back to the initial tetrahedral carbon with ring digit `1`. This yields `*NC1([O-])NNC(=O)c2ccccc21`.

planner_metadata.distinctiveness_rationale: This is the direct graph-to-SMILES route: extract the molecular graph from the drawing after deleting the mechanistic arrows, then choose one traversal through the fused heterocycle. It is sufficient because the task has a single structural interpretation rather than multiple independent solution paths.
planner_metadata.image_role: Read the skeletal structure in the image: a benzene ring fused to a heterocyclic carbonyl ring, a top carbonyl C=O, two adjacent right-side NH atoms, a central tetrahedral carbon bearing an O− substituent and an NH-R substituent, plus curved arrows that are to be ignored.
planner_metadata.text_role: Use the question text to know that the requested output is the SMILES expression of the transition-state structure and that the arrows in the drawing must be ignored.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: Use standard SMILES rules: represent unspecified R as wildcard `*`, neutral amine nitrogens as `N`, anionic oxygen as `[O-]`, carbonyl as `C(=O)`, aromatic benzene atoms as lowercase `c`, and ring closures/fusion with matching ring digits.
